question: The length of the badminton court for singles is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is 13.40 m.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A badminton court is a rectangular flat surface, and for a singles match its length is 13.40 m (44 feet). (बैडमिंटन कोर्ट — 13.40 मीटर)

 

• The width of the singles court is 5.18 m, while for doubles the width increases to 6.1 m, though the length remains the same 13.40 m for both formats.

 

• The net height at the centre of the court is 1.524 m (5 ft), and at the posts it is 1.55 m.

 

• Badminton is governed internationally by the Badminton World Federation (BWF), headquartered in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The doubles long service line is 0.76 m from the back boundary line, while in singles the back boundary line itself serves as the long service line.

 

• A badminton racket weighs approximately 70-95 grams, and the feathered shuttlecock weighs about 4.74-5.50 grams.

 

NOTE

 

• 13.44 m (Option 1): This does not correspond to the official BWF measurement of a badminton court.

 

• 13.55 m (Option 2): This is also an incorrect measurement, not matching the official specification.

 

• 14 m (Option 3): This is close to, but not the exact, official length of a badminton court.

question: Who is the Administrative Head of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Comptroller and Auditor General.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) is the constitutional authority who heads the Indian Audit and Accounts Department (IAAD) and audits all receipts and expenditure of the Union and State governments. (नियंत्रक एवं महालेखा परीक्षक — भारतीय लेखा परीक्षा विभाग के प्रशासनिक प्रमुख)

 

• The office of the CAG is established under Article 148 of the Constitution of India and the CAG is appointed by the President of India.

 

• The CAG's reports relating to the accounts of the Union/States are submitted to the President/Governor and examined by the Public Accounts Committee (PAC).

 

• The CAG holds office for a term of 6 years or until the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier, and can be removed only in the same manner as a Supreme Court judge.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The CAG is often described as the guardian of the public purse and upholds the financial accountability system of the Union and the States.

 

• The role and powers of the CAG are laid down in Part V, Chapter V (Articles 148-151) of the Constitution and the CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971.

 

NOTE

 

• Accountant General (Option 1): This officer heads the accounts and audit office at the state level, functioning under the overall authority of the CAG, not as the department's head.

 

• Principal Accountant General (Option 2): This is a senior state-level officer subordinate to the CAG, not the department's administrative head.

 

• Director General (Option 3): This is one of several departmental designations within the IAAD, not its overall administrative head.

question: Which of the following is the largest pan-India scheme to strengthen health care infrastructure across the country with focus on primary, secondary and tertiary care services?
solution_text:
The correct answer is PM-ABHIM.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Pradhan Mantri Ayushman Bharat Health Infrastructure Mission (PM-ABHIM) was launched on 25 October 2021 and is the largest pan-India scheme to strengthen health care infrastructure with focus on primary, secondary and tertiary care. (प्रधानमंत्री-आयुष्मान भारत स्वास्थ्य अवसंरचना मिशन — PM-ABHIM)

 

• It has an outlay of about ₹64,180 crore for the period 2021-22 to 2025-26, aiming to fill critical gaps in public health infrastructure, especially in rural and underserved areas.

 

• The scheme provides for setting up critical care hospital blocks, Integrated District Public Health Laboratories, Block Public Health Units, and strengthening of the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC).

 

• It is implemented by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and complements the existing National Health Mission.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Ayushman Bharat has two components: PM-JAY (health insurance) and Health and Wellness Centres, both launched in 2018.

 

• LaQshya (Labour Room Quality Improvement Initiative) aims to improve quality of care in labour rooms and maternity operation theatres.

 

NOTE

 

• LaQshya (Option 1): This scheme focuses specifically on improving the quality of care during delivery in labour rooms, not on overall pan-India health infrastructure.

 

• AB-PMJAY (Option 2): This is a health insurance scheme providing cashless treatment coverage of ₹5 lakh per family per year, not an infrastructure-strengthening scheme.

 

• PM-MI (Option 4): There is no such standard, nationally recognised health infrastructure scheme by this name.

question: Which of the following festivals is associated with the term ‘ties of protection’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Raksha Bandhan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Raksha Bandhan literally means the 'tie/knot of protection' (Raksha = protection, Bandhan = tie/bond), celebrating the bond between brothers and sisters. (रक्षा बंधन — सुरक्षा का बंधन)

 

• On this day a sister ties a sacred thread called a rakhi on her brother's wrist, symbolising her prayers for his well-being, while the brother pledges to protect her.

 

• It is celebrated on the full moon day (Purnima) of the Hindu month of Shravana, usually falling in August.

 

• Over time the festival has come to symbolise bonds of protection beyond biological siblings, including cousins, and even between soldiers and civilians.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bhai Dooj, celebrated during Diwali, is another Indian festival that similarly celebrates the brother-sister bond.

 

• Raksha Bandhan is celebrated across various regions of India under different regional names, such as Rakhi Purnima.

 

NOTE

 

• Baisakhi (Option 1): This is a harvest festival, primarily celebrated in Punjab, which also marks the formation of the Khalsa Panth by Guru Gobind Singh.

 

• Karwa Chauth (Option 2): This is a fast observed by married Hindu women for the safety and longevity of their husbands; it is not associated with 'ties of protection'.

 

• Chhath Pooja (Option 3): This is a festival dedicated to the worship of the Sun God (Surya) and Chhathi Maiya, prominently celebrated in Bihar, Jharkhand and eastern Uttar Pradesh.

question: In October 2021, 19-year-old ________ won the silver medal at the World Wrestling Championship.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Anshu Malik.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Anshu Malik won the silver medal in the women's 57 kg freestyle category at the 2021 World Wrestling Championships held in Oslo, Norway, in October 2021. (अंशु मलिक — विश्व कुश्ती चैंपियनशिप रजत पदक)

 

• With this achievement, she became the first Indian woman wrestler ever to win a medal at the World Wrestling Championships.

 

• She lost the final bout to Yui Susaki of Japan, a formidable and then-undefeated wrestler, settling for the silver medal.

 

• Anshu Malik hails from Nidani village, Jind district, Haryana, and comes from a family with a strong wrestling background.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• At the same 2021 World Championships, Sarita Mor won a bronze medal, contributing to India's best-ever showing by women wrestlers at that edition.

 

• Anshu Malik also represented India at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics and won a silver medal at the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham.

 

NOTE

 

• Seema Bisla (Option 2): She is an Indian wrestler who has competed at the World Championships and Commonwealth Games but did not win the silver medal referred to here.

 

• Sanju Devi (Option 3): She is not associated with winning a silver medal at the 2021 World Wrestling Championships.

 

• Sonam Malik (Option 4): She is an Indian wrestler who competed at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics but did not win this particular medal at the 2021 World Championships.

question: ________ emerged as the poorest state as per the first-ever Multi-dimensional Poverty Index (MPI) prepared by Niti Aayog and launched in November 2021.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• NITI Aayog released India's first-ever national Multi-dimensional Poverty Index (MPI) report, titled 'National MPI: Baseline Report', in November 2021. (बहुआयामी गरीबी सूचकांक — बिहार सर्वाधिक गरीब राज्य)

 

• As per this report, Bihar emerged as the poorest state in India, with roughly 51.91% of its population classified as multidimensionally poor.

 

• Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh followed as the next poorest large states, while Kerala recorded the lowest proportion of poor population.

 

• The index was based on the NFHS-4 (2015-16) data and uses three dimensions — health, education, and standard of living — comprising 12 indicators, aligned with the SDGs.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The MPI methodology was developed jointly by the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI) and the UNDP.

 

• Among Union Territories, Kerala and Goa were among the best performers, while Dadra and Nagar Haveli had comparatively higher poverty.

 

NOTE

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 2): MP had a high poverty ratio and ranked among the poorest large states but was not ranked first.

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 3): UP also had a high proportion of multidimensionally poor population but ranked below Bihar.

 

• Mizoram (Option 4): Mizoram had one of the lowest poverty ratios among the North-eastern states, far from being the poorest.

question: The consumption of fixed capital is also known as _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is depreciation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Consumption of Fixed Capital (CFC), also known as depreciation, refers to the decline in the value of fixed capital assets (machinery, buildings, equipment) due to normal wear and tear, obsolescence, or accidental damage over an accounting period. (मूल्यह्रास — स्थायी पूंजी का उपभोग)

 

• It is deducted from Gross Investment to arrive at Net Investment: Net Investment = Gross Investment − Depreciation.

 

• Similarly, subtracting depreciation from Gross Domestic Product (GDP) gives Net Domestic Product (NDP).

 

• Depreciation is a non-cash expense and is provided for in national accounts to reflect the true economic value retained by capital assets.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Gross Investment refers to the total expenditure on capital goods before adjusting for depreciation, while Net Investment is what remains after accounting for it.

 

• In India, national income accounting is carried out by the National Statistical Office (NSO), under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.

 

NOTE

 

• Net investment (Option 2): This is the amount remaining after deducting depreciation from gross investment; it is not itself another name for depreciation.

 

• Appreciation (Option 3): This refers to an *increase* in the value of an asset, the opposite of depreciation.

 

• Gross investment (Option 4): This is the total investment made before adjusting for the consumption of fixed capital, not the same concept as depreciation.

question: The Vedic Aryans lived in the area called Sapt-Sindhu, which means area drained by seven rivers. One of the rivers among the seven is Jhelum. What was its ancient name?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vitasta.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The river Jhelum was known as Vitasta in the Vedic period; it is mentioned in the Rigveda as one of the rivers of the Sapta-Sindhu (land of seven rivers) region. (वितस्ता — झेलम नदी का प्राचीन नाम)

 

• The Sapta-Sindhu region referred to the area drained by the Sindhu (Indus) and its tributaries, forming the core geographical setting of the Rigvedic period.

 

• The seven rivers were Sindhu (Indus), Vitasta (Jhelum), Askini (Chenab), Parushni (Ravi), Vipash (Beas), Shutudri (Sutlej), and the Sarasvati.

 

• These rivers of present-day Punjab and its neighbourhood formed the heartland of early Vedic civilisation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The river Sarasvati, mentioned prominently in the Rigveda as a mighty river, is believed by many scholars to have dried up over time, corresponding to the present-day Ghaggar-Hakra system.

 

• The Rigveda is the oldest of the four Vedas and provides the primary source of information about the geography and society of the Early Vedic period.

 

NOTE

 

• Askini (Option 1): This was the ancient name of the river Chenab, not Jhelum.

 

• Parushni (Option 2): This was the ancient name of the river Ravi, famous as the site of the Battle of the Ten Kings (Dasarajna).

 

• Vipash (Option 3): This was the ancient name of the river Beas, not Jhelum.

question: In Chola administration, ________ was the assembly in the villages which were inhabited predominantly by the Brahmanas.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sabha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under Chola administration, the Sabha (or Mahasabha) was the village assembly found in Brahmadeya/agrahara villages — villages inhabited predominantly by Brahmanas and gifted to them, often tax-free. (सभा — ब्राह्मण बहुल ग्रामों की सभा)

 

• The Sabha operated through several specialised committees (variyams), such as the Tank committee (Eri-variyam) and Garden committee (Thottavariyam), each handling specific local administrative functions.

 

• Detailed information about the functioning of the Sabha comes from the famous Uttiramerur inscriptions of the reign of Parantaka I, describing the election process of committee members.

 

• Members of the Sabha were typically chosen by lottery (Kudavolai system) from among eligible property-owning Brahmana residents.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Ur was the general assembly of ordinary (non-Brahmadeya) villages, open to all male tax-paying residents.

 

• The Nagaram was the assembly associated with trade and merchant activity, typically found in towns with a sizeable mercantile population.

 

NOTE

 

• Ur (Option 1): This was the general village assembly for non-Brahmadeya villages comprising the tax-paying residents, not specifically Brahmana-dominated villages.

 

• Khilya (Option 2): This term is not a standard Chola village assembly; it does not fit the administrative terminology of the period.

 

• Nagaram (Option 3): This was the assembly of merchants/traders in commercial towns, not a Brahmana-village assembly.

question: Which of the following states is NOT a part of the Tapi Basin?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Tapi (Tapti) river basin extends over only three states — Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, and Gujarat; Rajasthan is not part of the Tapi basin. (तापी बेसिन — महाराष्ट्र, मध्य प्रदेश, गुजरात)

 

• Maharashtra accounts for nearly 80% of the basin area, making it by far the largest contributor, followed by Madhya Pradesh and then Gujarat.

 

• The Tapi river originates near Multai in the Betul district of Madhya Pradesh and flows westward for about 724 km before draining into the Gulf of Khambhat (Arabian Sea) near Surat.

 

• Along with the Narmada, the Tapi is one of the few major Indian rivers that flows from east to west, following a rift valley between the Satpura and Satmala hill ranges.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Major tributaries of the Tapi include the Purna, Girna, Panzara, and Waghur rivers.

 

• The city of Surat in Gujarat is situated on the banks of the Tapi river, near its mouth.

 

NOTE

 

• Maharashtra (Option 2): It is very much part of the Tapi basin, in fact contributing the largest share of the drainage area.

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 3): The river originates in this state (Betul district) and forms part of the basin.

 

• Gujarat (Option 4): The river flows through this state before draining into the Arabian Sea, and is thus part of the basin.

question: Which of the following is used as a cooling medium for the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) and the superconducting magnets in MRI scanners and NMR spectrometers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Helium.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Liquid helium is used as the cooling medium (cryogen) for the superconducting magnets in the Large Hadron Collider (LHC), as well as in MRI scanners and NMR spectrometers. (हीलियम — शीतलक माध्यम)

 

• Helium has the lowest boiling point of any element (-269°C / 4.2 K), allowing it to keep superconducting magnet coils cold enough to maintain zero electrical resistance.

 

• At the LHC (CERN), superconducting magnets are cooled using liquid helium to about 1.9 K, colder than outer space, to generate the powerful magnetic fields needed to bend particle beams.

 

• In MRI (Magnetic Resonance Imaging) machines, liquid helium cools the superconducting magnet coils that generate the strong, stable magnetic field required for imaging.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Helium is the second most abundant element in the universe after hydrogen but is comparatively rare on Earth.

 

• Helium is chemically inert (a noble gas), non-flammable, and non-toxic, making it especially suitable as a coolant in sensitive scientific equipment.

 

NOTE

 

• Neon (Option 1): Though also a noble gas, Neon is not used as the primary cooling medium for these superconducting systems.

 

• Chlorine (Option 2): Chlorine is a reactive halogen gas and is not used as a coolant in such systems.

 

• Argon (Option 3): Argon is used as an inert shielding gas in various industrial applications, but not as the coolant for LHC magnets or MRI scanners.

question: In 2018, Google Doodle celebrated the 100th birthday of Mrinalini Sarabhai. She is an exponent of which of the following dance forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam and Kathakali.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mrinalini Sarabhai (1918-2016) was a renowned Indian classical dancer and choreographer, celebrated as an exponent of Bharatanatyam and Kathakali. (मृणालिणी साराभाई — भरतनाट्यम और कथकली)

 

• On 11 May 2018, Google Doodle commemorated her 100th birth anniversary, honouring her contributions to Indian classical dance.

 

• She founded the Darpana Academy of Performing Arts in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, in 1949, which remains a major centre for dance, music, drama and puppetry.

 

• She was married to renowned scientist Dr. Vikram Sarabhai, and their daughter, Mallika Sarabhai, is also an acclaimed classical dancer and activist.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Mrinalini Sarabhai was honoured with the Padma Bhushan (1992) for her contribution to the arts.

 

• She trained under legendary gurus and studied various classical dance forms during her career, but is most prominently identified with Bharatanatyam and Kathakali.

 

NOTE

 

• Odissi and Kathak (Option 2): These are separate classical dance forms not primarily associated with Mrinalini Sarabhai's legacy.

 

• Kuchipudi and Bharatanatyam (Option 3): While she was proficient in Bharatanatyam, she was not primarily known for Kuchipudi.

 

• Yakshagana (Option 4): This is a theatre form from coastal Karnataka, unrelated to Mrinalini Sarabhai's principal dance disciplines.

question: Bharatanatyam expresses South Indian religious themes and spiritual ideas of _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shaivism.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bharatanatyam, one of the oldest classical dance forms of India, originated in the temples of Tamil Nadu and predominantly expresses South Indian religious themes and spiritual ideas rooted in Shaivism — the worship of Lord Shiva. (भरतनाट्यम — शैव मत)

 

• The dance form has historically been closely linked to temple worship, with Devadasis performing it as an offering to deities, especially Shiva, in temples like the Thanjavur Brihadeeswarar Temple.

 

• Shiva is depicted as Nataraja, the Cosmic Dancer, who is considered the god of dance and the presiding deity of Bharatanatyam.

 

• The dance form is codified based on the ancient treatise Natya Shastra, attributed to sage Bharata Muni.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Modern Bharatanatyam owes much of its systematisation to the Tanjore Quartet in the 19th century.

 

• Other classical dance forms of India also draw on religious themes: Odissi is closely associated with Vaishnavism (Lord Jagannath).

 

NOTE

 

• Sufism (Option 1): This is a mystical dimension of Islam and is not the religious basis of Bharatanatyam.

 

• Buddhism (Option 3): While Buddhist themes appear in some Indian art forms, Bharatanatyam's core themes are rooted in Shaivism, not Buddhism.

 

• Jainism (Option 4): Jain themes are prominent in art forms like those at Ellora and Khajuraho, but not the principal spiritual basis of Bharatanatyam.

question: Who among the following musicians is popular for his mastery over the musical instrument Sitar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Vilayat Khan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ustad Vilayat Khan (1928-2004) was one of the most celebrated Sitar maestros of India, renowned for developing the Gayaki Ang style of sitar playing that mimics vocal music. (उस्ताद विलायत खान — सितार वादक)

 

• He belonged to the Imdadkhani (Etawah) gharana of sitar playing and was known for his emotive and melodious rendering of ragas.

 

• He was honoured with the Padma Bhushan and Padma Vibhushan, though he famously declined to accept them at certain points in his career.

 

• His disciples and successors, including his sons Shujaat Khan and others, have carried forward his distinctive sitar style.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Pandit Ravi Shankar is another globally renowned sitar maestro, credited with popularising Indian classical music worldwide.

 

• The Sitar is a plucked stringed instrument central to Hindustani classical music, distinct from the Sarod, which is fretless and played with a plectrum.

 

NOTE

 

• Ali Akbar Khan (Option 1): He was a legendary Sarod maestro, not a sitar player.

 

• Bahadur Khan (Option 3): He was also known for playing the Sarod, not the sitar.

 

• Amjad Ali Khan (Option 4): He is one of India's foremost Sarod players, not a sitarist.

question: Which of the following countries was the host of AFC Women's Asia Cup Football–2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The AFC Women's Asian Cup 2022 was hosted by India, held from 20 January to 6 February 2022, marking the first time India hosted this tournament. (एएफसी महिला एशियन कप 2022 — भारत मेज़बान)

 

• Matches were played in stadiums in Mumbai, Navi Mumbai, and Pune (Maharashtra).

 

• China won the tournament, defeating South Korea in the final to claim their 9th title.

 

• The tournament also served as the AFC qualifying tournament for the 2023 FIFA Women's World Cup, co-hosted by Australia and New Zealand.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Indian women's football team also participated as hosts but did not advance beyond the group stage.

 

• The previous edition, AFC Women's Asian Cup 2018, was won by Japan, held in Jordan.

 

NOTE

 

• Japan (Option 1): Japan is a former host (2014) and champion of the AFC Women's Asian Cup, but not the host of the 2022 edition.

 

• Bangladesh (Option 2): Bangladesh has hosted age-group and SAFF tournaments, but not the AFC Women's Asian Cup 2022.

 

• China (Option 4): China won the 2022 tournament but did not host it; India was the host.

question: Ms Bhakti Pradip Kulkarni was conferred with the Arjuna Award 2022 for her outstanding contribution in which of the following sports?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chess.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Bhakti Pradip Kulkarni, an Indian Woman Grandmaster (WGM) in chess, was conferred with the Arjuna Award 2022 for her outstanding contribution to the sport of Chess. (भक्ति कुलकर्णी — अर्जुन पुरस्कार, शतरंज)

 

• She received the award alongside young chess prodigy R. Praggnanandhaa, who was also honoured with the Arjuna Award in the same year for chess.

 

• Bhakti Kulkarni hails from Goa and has represented India at multiple Chess Olympiads.

 

• The Arjuna Award is conferred by the Government of India for outstanding achievement in sports, given by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Arjuna Award was instituted in 1961 and is one of the oldest sports honours in India.

 

• India's chess achievements have grown significantly, with players like Viswanathan Anand, D. Gukesh, and R. Praggnanandhaa bringing international recognition to the sport.

 

NOTE

 

• Table Tennis (Option 1): Bhakti Kulkarni's achievements were in chess, not table tennis.

 

• Badminton (Option 3): She is not associated with badminton; her recognition was for chess.

 

• Wrestling (Option 4): She was honoured for chess, not wrestling.

question: Who among the following was the founder of ‘Tiger Legion' or ‘Free India Legion'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Subhas Chandra Bose.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Subhas Chandra Bose founded the 'Free India Legion' (Freies Indien Legion), also known as the 'Tiger Legion', in Nazi Germany in 1941, comprising Indian prisoners of war and volunteers to fight for India's independence. (स्वतंत्र भारत सेना / टाइगर लीजन — सुभाष चंद्र बोस)

 

• Bose had travelled to Germany in 1941 seeking Axis support against British rule and set up this legion under German patronage, though it ultimately saw limited combat action.

 

• He later moved to Southeast Asia in 1943, where he took leadership of the Indian National Army (Azad Hind Fauj), originally raised by Rash Behari Bose, and formed the Azad Hind (Provisional Government of Free India).

 

• The Legion's flag and insignia featured a leaping tiger, giving it the popular name 'Tiger Legion'.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Subhas Chandra Bose gave the famous slogan 'Give me blood, and I shall give you freedom' and adopted the title 'Netaji'.

 

• He is also credited with popularising the slogan 'Jai Hind'.

 

NOTE

 

• Vinayak Damodar Savarkar (Option 1): He was a revolutionary and ideologue associated with Hindutva, not the founder of the Free India Legion.

 

• Sohan Singh Bhakhna (Option 3): He was a founding leader of the Ghadar Party, not the Free India Legion.

 

• Lala Hardayal (Option 4): He was another key founder of the Ghadar Party in the USA, unrelated to the Free India Legion.

question: Name a reproductive strategy in which parasites take advantage of the care of other individuals of the same species or different species to raise their young.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Brood parasitism.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Brood parasitism is a reproductive strategy in which an organism lays its eggs in the nest of another individual, of the same or a different species, relying on the host to raise its young. (ब्रूड परजीविता — अन्य जीवों द्वारा पालन-पोषण)

 

• A classic example is the Common Cuckoo (Cuculus canorus), which lays its eggs in the nests of other bird species; the host bird unknowingly raises the cuckoo chick, often at the expense of its own offspring.

 

• Among Indian birds, the Asian Koel exhibits brood parasitism, commonly laying eggs in the nests of crows.

 

• This strategy reduces the parental investment required from the parasitic species while ensuring survival of its offspring through the host's care.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Brood parasitism can be interspecific (between different species, e.g., cuckoo and host bird) or intraspecific (within the same species, seen in some ducks and insects).

 

• Some brood parasite hatchlings, like cuckoo chicks, actively push the host's own eggs or chicks out of the nest to eliminate competition.

 

NOTE

 

• Sexual parasitism (Option 2): This refers to a mating strategy, seen for example in anglerfish, where a male permanently fuses to a female, not related to offspring-rearing by others.

 

• Klepto parasitism (Option 3): This refers to stealing food or resources already collected by another organism (e.g., frigatebirds stealing food from other seabirds), not related to raising young.

 

• Competitive parasitism (Option 4): This is not a standard recognised biological term for this reproductive strategy.

question:
On the basis of tribal population (2011), identify the option that arranges the following states in ascending order.

A. Madhya Pradesh

B. Maharashtra

C. Odisha
solution_text:
The correct answer is (C), (B), (A).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the 2011 Census, among these three states, Odisha had the smallest Scheduled Tribe (ST) population, followed by Maharashtra, with Madhya Pradesh having the largest — giving the ascending order Odisha, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh. (जनजातीय जनसंख्या 2011 — मध्य प्रदेश सर्वाधिक)

 

• Madhya Pradesh has the largest Scheduled Tribe population of any state in India, at approximately 1.53 crore (15.3 million) as per the 2011 Census.

 

• Maharashtra's ST population was approximately 1.05 crore (10.5 million), ranking second.

 

• Odisha's ST population was approximately 95 lakh (9.5 million), the smallest of the three states listed.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• As per the 2011 Census, India's Scheduled Tribe population was about 10.43 crore, constituting 8.6% of the total population.

 

• In terms of the proportion of ST population to a state's total population (rather than absolute numbers), North-eastern states like Mizoram and Lakshadweep (UT) rank highest.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 are incorrect because they do not reflect the correct ascending order of ST population — Madhya Pradesh must appear last (largest), and Odisha must appear first (smallest), which only Option 1 satisfies.

question: In which industrial policy was the investment limit for tiny industry/unit increased to ₹2 lakh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1980.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Industrial Policy Statement of 1980 revised the investment limit for tiny units upward, increasing it to ₹2 lakh (from the earlier limit set under the 1977 policy). (औद्योगिक नीति 1980 — लघु इकाई निवेश सीमा ₹2 लाख)

 

• The Industrial Policy of 1980 aimed at promoting balanced regional development, encouraging small-scale and tiny sectors, and reviving sick industrial units.

 

• It also emphasised the concept of 'District Industries Centres (DICs)', which had been introduced under the 1977 policy, for promoting small and village industries.

 

• Successive policies continued to revise investment ceilings for small-scale and tiny units in line with inflation and industrial growth needs.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Industrial Policy Resolution, 1956, is regarded as the basic economic policy framework of India for a long period, classifying industries into three categories based on the role of the state.

 

• The New Industrial Policy of 1991 brought about liberalisation, delicensing of most industries, and reduced the role of the public sector, marking a major shift from earlier policies.

 

NOTE

 

• 1977 (Option 1): The Industrial Policy of 1977 focused on small-scale and cottage industries and introduced the concept of tiny units, but the increase to ₹2 lakh came under the 1980 policy.

 

• 1991 (Option 2): This policy is known for liberalisation and delicensing, not specifically for revising the tiny unit investment limit to ₹2 lakh.

 

• 1956 (Option 4): This early policy resolution classified industries by sector but did not set this specific investment limit for tiny units.

question: Which scientist thought of the concept of steady state of the universe?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Fred Hoyle.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Steady State Theory of the universe was proposed in 1948 by British astronomer Fred Hoyle, along with Hermann Bondi and Thomas Gold. (स्थिर अवस्था सिद्धांत — फ्रेड हॉयल)

 

• The theory proposed that the universe has no beginning and no end in time, and that as the universe expands, new matter is continuously created to keep its overall density constant — maintaining a 'steady state'.

 

• Fred Hoyle is also credited with coining the term 'Big Bang', ironically while criticising the rival theory during a BBC radio broadcast in 1949.

 

• The Steady State Theory eventually lost favour after the discovery of the Cosmic Microwave Background Radiation (CMBR) in 1965, which provided strong evidence supporting the Big Bang theory instead.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Edwin Hubble discovered that the universe is expanding, laying observational groundwork for the Big Bang theory, through what is known as Hubble's Law.

 

• The Big Bang theory, first proposed by Georges Lemaître, is the currently accepted scientific explanation for the origin of the universe.

 

NOTE

 

• Harold Jeffrey (Option 1): He was a geophysicist and mathematician known for his work on Earth's structure and seismology, not the Steady State Theory.

 

• Edwin Hubble (Option 2): He is known for discovering the expansion of the universe (Hubble's Law), not for proposing the Steady State Theory.

 

• Pierre-Simon Laplace (Option 4): He was a mathematician and astronomer known for his work on celestial mechanics and probability, not the Steady State Theory.

question:
Match the columns.

Column-A (Class): i. Chlorophyceae   ii. Phaeophyceae   iii. Rhodophyceae   iv. Cyanophyceae

Column-B (Common name): a. Brown algae   b. Green algae   c. Blue-green algae   d. Red algae
solution_text:
The correct answer is i-b, ii-a, iii-d, iv-c.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chlorophyceae (i) are commonly known as Green algae (b), as they contain chlorophyll a and b as the dominant pigments, giving them a green colour. (शैवाल वर्गीकरण — क्लोरोफाइसी: हरित शैवाल)

 

• Phaeophyceae (ii) are commonly known as Brown algae (a), owing to the dominance of the pigment fucoxanthin, which masks the green chlorophyll.

 

• Rhodophyceae (iii) are commonly known as Red algae (d), due to the presence of the red pigment r-phycoerythrin.

 

• Cyanophyceae (iv), also called blue-green algae (c), are actually photosynthetic prokaryotes (cyanobacteria) containing chlorophyll a and phycocyanin.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Chlorophyceae members mostly occur in fresh water, e.g., Chlamydomonas, Volvox, Ulothrix, Spirogyra.

 

• Rhodophyceae (red algae) are predominantly marine and include forms like Polysiphonia, Porphyra, and Gracilaria, some of which are commercially important as sources of agar.

 

NOTE

 

• Option 1 (i-b, ii-c, iii-a, iv-d): Incorrectly pairs Phaeophyceae with blue-green algae and Rhodophyceae with brown algae, which is wrong.

 

• Option 3 (i-d, ii-c, iii-b, iv-a): Incorrectly pairs Chlorophyceae with red algae and other mismatches that do not correspond to the correct common names.

 

• Option 4 (i-a, ii-b, iii-c, iv-d): Incorrectly pairs Chlorophyceae with brown algae and Phaeophyceae with green algae, which is wrong.

question: Ryotwari system of revenue collection in India, introduced by the British, was based on the _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ricardian theory of rent.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Ryotwari system, introduced primarily by Thomas Munro and Alexander Read in the Madras and Bombay Presidencies, was based on the Ricardian theory of rent, developed by economist David Ricardo. (रैयतवाड़ी व्यवस्था — रिकार्डो का लगान सिद्धांत)

 

• Under this system, the revenue settlement was made directly with the individual cultivator (ryot), rather than through intermediaries like zamindars.

 

• According to Ricardo's theory of rent, revenue was to be assessed based on the differential fertility of land, with the state claiming a share of the surplus produce over and above the cost of cultivation.

 

• The system was periodically revised, and land revenue was reassessed every 20-30 years based on soil quality, irrigation facilities, and crop patterns.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The other major land revenue systems introduced by the British were the Permanent Settlement (Zamindari System), introduced by Lord Cornwallis in 1793, and the Mahalwari System, prevalent in parts of North India.

 

• Under Zamindari settlement, zamindars acted as intermediaries responsible for revenue collection from cultivators, unlike Ryotwari, where the state dealt directly with farmers.

 

NOTE

 

• Smith's theory of rent (Option 1): Adam Smith's economic theories primarily concern the division of labour and free markets, not the specific basis of the Ryotwari system.

 

• Malthusian theory of rent (Option 3): Thomas Malthus is chiefly known for his population theory, not the theoretical basis of Ryotwari settlement.

 

• Marx's theory of rent (Option 4): Karl Marx's theory of rent relates to his broader critique of capitalism and surplus value, and was not the basis for the Ryotwari system.

question: Who received the Nobel Prize in 1901 for ‘recognition of the extraordinary services rendered by the discovery of the laws of chemical dynamics and osmotic pressure in solutions’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Jacobus Henricus van 't Hoff.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Jacobus Henricus van 't Hoff, a Dutch chemist, was awarded the very first Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1901 for discovering the laws of chemical dynamics and osmotic pressure in solutions. (जैकबस हेनरिकस वांट हॉफ — प्रथम रसायन विज्ञान नोबेल पुरस्कार, 1901)

 

• His work laid the foundation of physical chemistry, particularly in the study of reaction rates (chemical kinetics) and the behaviour of dilute solutions.

 

• Van 't Hoff formulated the van 't Hoff equation, relating osmotic pressure to solute concentration, and contributed significantly to stereochemistry, including the concept of the tetrahedral carbon atom.

 

• The Nobel Prize in Chemistry is awarded annually by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences, and 1901 marked the very first year the Nobel Prizes were awarded across all categories.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen received the first-ever Nobel Prize in Physics in 1901, for his discovery of X-rays.

 

• Emil von Behring received the first Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in 1901, for his work on serum therapy against diphtheria.

 

NOTE

 

• Hermann Emil Fischer (Option 1): He won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1902 for his work on sugar and purine synthesis, not in 1901.

 

• Svante August Arrhenius (Option 3): He won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1903 for his theory of electrolytic dissociation, not in 1901.

 

• Henri Moissan (Option 4): He won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1906 for isolating fluorine and developing the electric furnace, not in 1901.

question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution are related to citizenship?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Articles 5 to 11.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Articles 5 to 11 of the Indian Constitution, contained in Part II, deal with the subject of Citizenship. (अनुच्छेद 5 से 11 — नागरिकता)

 

• Article 5 defines citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution; Article 6 deals with citizenship rights of persons who migrated from Pakistan; Article 7 covers persons who migrated to Pakistan.

 

• Article 8 relates to citizenship rights of persons of Indian origin residing outside India; Article 9 provides that a person voluntarily acquiring citizenship of a foreign state will not be an Indian citizen.

 

• Article 10 provides for continuance of citizenship rights, while Article 11 empowers Parliament to regulate citizenship by law — leading to the enactment of the Citizenship Act, 1955.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India follows a single citizenship model, unlike countries with dual citizenship (federal and state), meaning all Indians are citizens of India regardless of the state they reside in.

 

• The Citizenship Act, 1955 and its subsequent amendments (including the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019) further elaborate provisions relating to acquisition and termination of Indian citizenship.

 

NOTE

 

• Articles 15 to 21 (Option 1): These articles fall under Part III (Fundamental Rights), covering rights such as equality, non-discrimination, freedom, and protection of life and personal liberty — not citizenship.

 

• Articles 2 to 4 (Option 3): These articles deal with the admission/establishment of new states and alteration of areas, boundaries, or names of existing states, not citizenship.

 

• Articles 25 to 31 (Option 4): These articles primarily relate to the Right to Freedom of Religion and, in the case of Article 31 (since repealed), the Right to Property — not citizenship.
